sources.title: Egypt fears escalation in Iran war would be more destructive, foreign minister says
Egyptian foreign minister 'extremely worried' US-Iran escalation will have major impact on Mideast

en.title: Egyptian foreign minister warns US‑Iran escalation will be more destructive
en.dek: Badr Abdelatty said he was extremely worried that a new US‑Iran conflict would be more destructive and have a major impact, speaking at the IISS Manama Dialogue.
facts: Badr Abdelatty said he was extremely worried about a new US‑Iran escalation.
He warned the second round would be more dangerous and destructive.
The statement was made at the IISS Manama Dialogue security summit in Bahrain.
An interim agreement reached in June failed to secure a lasting ceasefire or restore shipping through the Strait of Hormuz.
Qatari mediators returned to Tehran to broker a deal, but sides remain divided over priorities.
body: Badr Abdelatty, Egypt's foreign minister, said on Saturday that he was extremely worried about a new escalation between the United States and Iran, and that the second round would be more dangerous and destructive.
The statement was made at the IISS Manama Dialogue security summit in Bahrain, which was held in Bahrain.

An interim agreement reached in June failed to secure a lasting ceasefire or restore normal shipping through the Strait of Hormuz. Iran has since proposed that Washington lift its blockade of Iranian ports in exchange for Tehran reopening the waterway within seven days.

Qatari mediators returned to Tehran on Friday in a renewed effort to broker a deal. However, the sides remain divided over whether nuclear negotiations or relief from the blockade and oil sanctions should come first.
en.context: The United States and Iran have been in conflict over nuclear negotiations and sanctions. A June interim agreement failed to secure a lasting ceasefire. Qatar has been mediating attempts to resolve the dispute.
en.imageCaption: US President Donald Trump and Egyptian President Abdel Fattah el-Sisi meet ahead of a world leaders' summit on ending the Gaza war, amid a US-brokered prisoner-hostage swap and ceasefire deal between Israel and Hamas, in Sharm El-Sheikh, Egypt, October 13, 2025.
